guarantees: state is never communicated by color alone
confidence renders as bands, never decimals
focus is never dropped: when a control goes away after use, focus moves to what replaced it

components.d: The review queue for background agents.
p: items:InboxItem[]
onOpen?:(id: string) => void // Called when the human opens a run for review
label?:string
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: each run is a button in tab order.
a.sr: a list named by `label`; each button reads the title, summary, what it waits on, and its status in words.
a.m: rows fade in and out; nothing moves on its own.
a.h: pass `onOpen`, or the rows are buttons that do nothing; order is yours, but put runs that need the person first.

components.d: The team sheet for multi-agent runs: who's working, who's waiting, who's blocked, and on what.
p: agents:RosterAgent[]
label?:string
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: nothing to operate; it is a read-only list.
a.sr: a list named by `label`; each agent's state reads in words (Working, Waiting, Blocked, Idle).
a.m: the working pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: keep agent ids stable across updates; keep `activity` to one short line.

components.d: The agent's plan, made visible: what it will do, what it's doing, what's done, and what broke.
p: label?:string // Short label for the overall plan, e.g. "Booking your trip"
tasks:AgentTask[]
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: nothing to operate; it is a read-only list.
a.sr: a list named by `label`; every step starts with its status in words (Not started, Working on, Done, Failed), and a failed step keeps its error.
a.m: the active step's pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: pass `label` so the list has a name; keep task titles unique (they key the rows).

components.d: An inline permission request: the agent states what it wants to do, shows the exact scope, and waits.
p: title:string // Plain-language request, e.g. "Send the Q3 summary email?"
reason?:string // Why the agent wants to do this
scope:ScopeItem[]
state?:ApprovalState // Controlled state; omit to let the component manage it
onApprove?:() => void
onDeny?:() => void
approveLabel?:string
denyLabel?:string
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Approve and Deny are ordinary buttons in tab order. Neither takes focus on its own, so a stray Enter can never consent.
a.sr: a group named by `title`; risky scope items say "Can't undo" in words. After a decision the receipt is announced and takes focus.
a.h: one gate per irreversible action, each with a distinct `title`; set `state` only from a real decision, never on mount.

components.d: The run's save points, newest at the top, and a way back to any of them.
p: checkpoints:CheckpointEntry[] // Newest first; the first entry is the current state
current?:string // Id of the checkpoint the run is at (defaults to the first)
onRestore?:(id: string) => void
confirming?:string | null // Controlled id of the checkpoint whose restore confirm is open
onConfirmingChange?:(id: string | null) => void
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Restore opens an inline confirm that takes focus; Escape keeps going.
a.sr: "You are here" reads in words; each Restore names its checkpoint, and the confirm says what will be undone.
a.m: opacity, scale and height on the confirm only.
a.h: give `undoes` for every checkpoint but the current one.

components.d: An inline source marker on a claim, and the drawer it opens.
p: index:number // 1-based number shown on the chip
source:Source
active?:boolean // Marks the chip whose source is open in the drawer
onOpen?:(index: number) => void
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: chips are buttons; Escape inside the drawer closes it.
a.sr: a chip reads "Source 1: <title>", and says when the source could not be reached; the drawer is a region named Sources.
a.h: one chip right after the sentence it supports; keep `index` matching the drawer's order.

components.d: One question the agent needs answered before it goes further, with the likely answers ready to tap and room for your own.
p: question:string
why?:string // Why the agent is asking, e.g. "This changes which files I edit"
options:ClarifyingOption[]
multi?:boolean // Allow choosing more than one option
allowOther?:boolean // Show a free-text "Something else" field
fallback?:string // What the agent does if the person skips; shows a Skip button when set
answer?:string[] | null // Controlled answer; omit to let the component manage it
onAnswer?:(answer: string[]) => void
onSkip?:() => void
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: each option is a button; keys 1 to 9 pick an option while it is open (not while typing); in multi mode options are checkboxes toggled with Space.
a.sr: the options are a list named by the question; once answered it reads "You chose …".
a.h: ask one question at a time; set `fallback` whenever the agent has a sensible default.

components.d: Honest uncertainty display: confidence as coarse bands, never decimal theater, paired with a verification affordance exactly when doubt is warranted.
p: claim:string // The claim being qualified, e.g. "This invoice matches PO #4412"
confidence:number // Model confidence 0..1; rendered as a band, not a number
basis?:string // What the confidence is based on, e.g. "3 matching fields, 1 OCR gap"
threshold?:number // Below this, the verify affordance becomes prominent (default 0.75)
onVerify?:() => void
verifyLabel?:string
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: the verify button is in tab order whenever it shows.
a.sr: the meter reads its band in words ("Medium confidence"), never a percentage; the claim and its basis read as text.
a.h: pass `confidence` from 0 to 1 and never print the number beside it; give `onVerify` whenever the person can check the claim.

components.d: A delegation contract's limits, made visible: tokens, spend, or time against their caps.
p: lines:BudgetLine[]
label?:string
onRaise?:(label: string) => void // Called when the human raises a cap after one is hit
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Raise cap is a button where a cap is reached and `onRaise` is given.
a.sr: each line is a progress bar named with its label, use and cap; the band reads in words.
a.m: the bar eases to its new width.
a.h: give lines distinct labels; pause the run at a cap before showing Raise.

components.d: An agent's proposed change to a file, reviewed hunk by hunk before it lands.
p: file:string // File path, e.g. "src/api/client.ts"
hunks:DiffHunk[]
decisions?:Record<string, HunkDecision> // Controlled decisions by hunk id; omit to let the card manage them
onDecide?:(id: string, decision: Exclude<HunkDecision, "pending">) => void
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Accept and Reject per hunk, and Accept all, are buttons in tab order.
a.sr: each button names its hunk ("Accept: Retry once on timeout"); removed and added lines are announced as such.
a.h: give every hunk a `summary`; apply a hunk only from onDecide.

components.d: The steering wheel and the brake for a running agent.
p: activity:string // What the agent is doing right now, e.g. "Comparing 14 flights"
elapsed?:number // Seconds elapsed in the run
state?:InterruptBarState
keptOnStop?:string // What was kept when stopped, e.g. "Search results saved"
onStop?:() => void
onSteer?:(message: string) => void // Called with the user's mid-run redirect
acknowledgment?:string // The agent's acknowledgment of the last steer, shown inline
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Stop is a button; the steer field sends on Enter.
a.sr: the steer acknowledgment and the stopped receipt are announced; after Stop, focus moves to the receipt.
a.m: the running pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: keep the bar on screen for the whole run, and set `acknowledgment` after onSteer so the person hears the steer was taken.

components.d: What the agent remembers about you, in its own words, with where each memory came from and a way to forget it.
p: memories:Memory[]
onForget?:(id: string) => void // Called once a forget is final (after the undo window)
paused?:boolean // Controlled paused state; omit to let the panel manage it
onPausedChange?:(paused: boolean) => void
undoMs?:number // How long Undo stays available, in ms (default 5000)
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Forget, Undo and the remembering switch are buttons.
a.sr: the switch reports on or off; forgetting is announced with its Undo.
a.m: rows collapse as they are forgotten.
a.h: forget for real only in onForget, which fires after the undo window.

components.d: The agent's plan, shown before it starts, as steps the person can drop or reword.
p: goal:string // What the plan is for, e.g. "Migrate billing to the new API"
steps:PlanStep[]
state?:PlanReviewState // Controlled state; omit to let the component manage it
onApprove?:(steps: PlanStep[]) => void // Called with the steps as edited, minus any the person dropped
onRevise?:() => void
dropped?:number[] // Controlled indexes of dropped steps; omit to let the component manage them
onDroppedChange?:(dropped: number[]) => void
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Edit opens an inline field (Enter or Escape to finish); Drop and Keep toggle a step; Approve plan submits.
a.sr: Edit and Drop name their step ("Drop step 3: Run the migration on staging"); dropped steps read "Dropped".
a.h: mark steps that change things outside the sandbox `risky`; run only the steps passed to onApprove.

components.d: The agent's thinking as a short list of steps the user can follow: open while it works, folded to a one-line summary when it's done, and never gone.
p: steps:ReasoningStep[]
streaming?:boolean // True while the agent is still thinking; the trace stays open
seconds?:number // Seconds spent thinking, shown in the folded summary
defaultOpen?:boolean // Start open after the run is done (default false: folds when finished)
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: the summary line is a button; Enter or Space opens and folds the steps.
a.sr: aria-expanded reports open or folded; each step starts with Now, Next or Done.
a.m: the active pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: write steps as actions ("Checking carry-on rules"), not raw model tokens; set `streaming` false when the answer lands, so it folds.

components.d: Who has the wheel, said plainly.
p: state:TakeoverState
reason?:string // What the agent is doing, or why it needs you, e.g. "Sign in to continue"
onTakeOver?:() => void
onHandBack?:() => void
privacyNote?:string // Shown while the person drives (default: the agent can't see the screen)
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: Take over and Hand back are buttons.
a.sr: a polite status region; every change of who is driving is announced, with the reason.
a.m: the driving pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: pin it to the surface the agent controls, and never hide Take over while the agent acts.

components.d: Shows an agent's tool call with legible, progressive disclosure.
p: name:string // Machine name of the tool, e.g. "search_flights"
intent:string // One-line human intent, e.g. "Searching SFO → JFK for Aug 12"
state:ToolCallState
args?:string // Pretty-printed arguments (JSON string or plain text)
detail?:string // Result or error detail
elapsed?:number // Seconds elapsed while running (optional)
className?:string // Extra classes merged onto the root element

a.k: the header is one button; Enter or Space shows and hides the arguments and result, when there are any.
a.sr: reads the tool name, the intent and the state in words ("Running · 3s", "Failed"); aria-expanded reports the disclosure.
a.m: the running pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
a.h: update `state` on the same card instead of swapping cards, so its place in the transcript holds; write `intent` in the person's words, not the API's.
